title: Elementary Idea of Valence Bond Theory
notes: **Valence Bond Theory (VBT):** a covalent bond forms when two atoms approach each other and their atomic orbitals overlap, with electrons pairing with opposite spins.
**Overlap condition:** greater overlap means stronger bond. Head-on overlap gives sigma ($\sigma$) bonds; sideways overlap gives pi ($\pi$) bonds.
**Sigma bond:** formed by end-to-end overlap of atomic orbitals along the internuclear axis. Free rotation is possible around a single $\sigma$ bond.

**Pi bond:** formed by sideways overlap of p-orbitals above and below the internuclear axis. Electron density is concentrated above and below the axis. Rotation is restricted because sideways overlap would break the bond.
**Bond strength order:** $\sigma$ bond is stronger than $\pi$ bond because end-on overlap is greater than sideways overlap.
